nghttp3_or_http3_library_present.answer: No library. nghttp3 source and binaries are not in the repository.
nghttp3_or_http3_library_present.note: Only ngtcp2 submodule build scripts and examples (ci/build_nghttp3.sh, cmake/FindLibnghttp3.cmake, examples/*) mention it; they are not built by this project. managed_components holds only dht, esp_idf_lib_helpers, cjson, ethernet_init, wolfssl.

estimates_http3.method: nghttp3 source is not available locally, so nothing could be built or measured. The nghttp3 range is a judgement anchored on the measured ngtcp2 archive in the QUIC build (171,628 B): nghttp3 is assumed to be roughly a third to under the same size as ngtcp2, widened for compiler options and which QPACK/HTTP/3 features are linked. Server-side ngtcp2 paths (server connection creation, Retry/token, path validation, connection IDs), wolfSSL server handshake with ECDSA signing, and the application code are rough guesses from general experience. The honest bounds are what matter, not the central value.

fits_in_current_free_app_space.answer: Only the optimistic end of the range would fit, with almost no margin; plan as not fitting.

partition_change.proposal: One larger factory app partition, for example 2048K (0x200000), which leaves about 0.2 to 0.4 MB headroom over the estimated image of about 1.72 to 1.86 MB. Flash is 8 MB and the partition table currently ends at 0x1B9000, so there is room.
tradeoffs: The current table has no OTA slots and no otadata (single factory app), so enlarging factory loses no OTA that exists today.

If OTA is wanted later, two equal app slots are needed (for example ota_0 and ota_1 at 2048K each plus otadata, about 4.2 MB of 8 MB), which still fits but doubles the app space and adds rollback complexity.

A new partition table has to be flashed (not only the app), moves the app offset, and changes every image hash, so it can only be a separate exploratory profile, never the frozen QUIC_PSN or TCP_TLS_PSN artifacts.
Keeping 1700K and removing features instead (for example the TCP_TLS code or logging) would not be a like-for-like build of the experiment firmware.

ram_bytes.basis: Free heap before connecting is measured (about 287 to 288 KB), but heap used by the existing MQTT/QUIC connection is not logged. The extra figures are guesses for one concurrent HTTP/3 connection with the QPACK dynamic table set to 0 and are not derived from a build.
ram_bytes.conclusion: Probably fits in RAM for one concurrent HTTP/3 connection next to the MQTT client; it must be confirmed by logging the minimum free heap.
